Asha (PM): Quick thread: customers pressed to clarify "commit slicing" (per-class reservations inside a single reserved pool) + fallback guarantees. Need product stance for next-week roadmap commit.
Lena (Eng): Two clean engineering paths: (A) soft-slicing: allocator biases tokens per class but allows spill; (B) hard-slicing: pinned quotas that strictly admit only if class has tokens. Soft is much faster to ship.
Marco (SRE): If we ship soft first, we must protect cluster from runaway burn. Required safety: per-tenant sliding-window token cap, lane-level circuit-breaker, and automatic demotion when burn_rate anomaly detected.
Priya (Sales): Customers want three things: predictable minimum throughput for a lane during bursts, ability to carry over unused lane credits, and explicit preemption rules. Sales will only sign enterprise deals with clear failure/credit language.
Owen (Solutions): Practical asks from pilots: (1) ability to pin X% of commit to "heavy" rerank requests, (2) a test harness for customers to validate behavior, (3) example configs we can run against their traces.
Lena (Eng): Minimal API sketch for soft-slice (for RFC):
```
PUT /reserved_pools/{id}/slices
{
  "slices": [
    {"name": "chat", "bias_pct": 60, "burst_ceiling_pct": 25},
    {"name": "embed", "bias_pct": 30, "burst_ceiling_pct": 15},
    {"name": "rerank", "bias_pct": 10, "burst_ceiling_pct": 10}
  ]
}
```
Lena (Eng): Hard-pins add admission-control hooks and enforcement; estimate soft-slice: 2 sprints (allocator + API + flags), hard-pins: 6-8 sprints (incl. tests & rollout).
Marco (SRE): Observability must include per-slice P50/P95/P99, burn-rate streams, fallback-trigger events, and a dedupe'd alert for cross-tenant noisy neighbors. No SLA sales until console shows these.
billing-bot: Note: meter schema v2 will include per-slice dimensions starting 2025-01-01.
Priya (Sales): Carryover is a dealbreaker for some customers. Options: (a) disabled by default, (b) premium opt-in with caps, (c) unlimited carryover at very high price. Which do we recommend?
Asha (PM): Proposal: GA defaults = soft-slicing self-serve, carryover disabled by default; pilot/enterprise = paid hard-pinned lanes with limited carryover. Telemetry gating required before any SLA.
Owen (Solutions): For migration we should provide a "slice simulator" tool: take historical trace, apply candidate slice config, show expected bleed/spill and latency distribution. Low effort to prototype.
Lena (Eng): Anti-abuse controls we should include: per-session token cap, anomaly detection (burst fingerprinting), and automatic weight decay for suspected abuse. We'll include a config toggle for strict-mode for pilot customers.
Marco (SRE): Runbook additions: fallback alert thresholds, remediation steps (throttle, demote, emergency-evict), and oncall escalation matrix. Must be reviewed by SRE leads before pilot.
Priya (Sales): I'll draft three offer templates: self-serve soft-slices (no SLA), enterprise pilot (hard-pin, limited carryover, test period), full SLA (strict pins + compensation matrix). Need exact numbers from eng.
Asha (PM): Acceptance criteria proposed for GA rollout:
- Soft-slicing API in Console + API docs.
- Per-slice telemetry live in Console and in billing exports.
- Safety nets: per-tenant cap and lane circuit-breaker live.
- Pilot bundle docs for hard-pin + carryover ready for enterprise sales.
Lena (Eng): Action items:
- RFC for allocator changes + API (due: next Tue).
- Prototype slice-simulator (due: next Fri).
Marco (SRE): Action items:
- Telemetry spec + canary alerts (due: 5 business days).
- Runbook drafts for fallback incidents (due: 7 business days).
Priya (Sales)/Owen (Solutions): Action items:
- Pilot package + sell sheet + legal slack for SLA wording (due: 10 business days).
Asha (PM): If there are no objections, we lock default to soft-slices for GA and proceed with pilot for hard-pins. Please react with :thumbsup: to approve or leave comments by EOD.
Lena (Eng): :thumbsup:
Marco (SRE): :thumbsup:
Owen (Solutions): :thumbsup: adding customer examples to pilot notes.
Priya (Sales): :thumbsup: will start legal loop.
Asha (PM): Thanks team. We'll review RFC in next product-allocator sync and publish roadmap milestone.
